newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices weaken in limited correction after rally.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices weaken in limited correction after rally.

text.p: Oil prices moved lower on Thursday after the market saw no further mileage from U.S. weekly energy stocks data which drove prices up the previous day.

World marker crude Brent Blend traded within a narrow range for much of the day before being knocked down in the late afternoon session, led by weaker crude futures on the larger New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX).
April Brent futures closed 23 cents down at the session low of $19.32 a barrel.
Futures brokers said they did not see much more downside potential for April Brent.
"There's still a feeling that the market is oversold. The funds are still short and they'll need to come in and cover," a futures broker said.

Oil prices had a volatile trading day on Wednesday, when front-month Brent closed 13 cents higher largely on the strength of a shortfall in U.S. gasoline stocks last week in the run-up to the spring driving season.

A threatened strike by oil export staff in Nigeria had been supportive but union leaders on Thursday played down the threat of an immediate strike and said they still hoped to negotiate with the government over back pay.

With holders of spot Iraqi crude oil trying to peddle their cargoes at below the official selling price agreed under the United Nations oil-for-food plan, crude oils of similar quality like Russian Urals have suffered.
A slide in world oil prices has meant Iraq has been offering spot cargoes in an effort to make up for a shortfall in revenue from contract sales under the U.N. deal.
But the latest crude sales contract approved by the U.N. should put Iraq at the monetary cap of $1 billion for the first 90 day period of the limited sales agreement, U.N. sources said on Thursday.
The 34th sales contract allows for Iraq to sell 40,000 barrels per day of crude oil to Indian Oil Corp. over a three month period.
The North Sea world benchmark crude Brent hit a low of $19.09 on Monday and is still around $5 a barrel below the high seen in January.
A mild winter in the northern hemisphere and rising Iraqi oil sales have combined to force prices down this year.
